subject: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Hi Alex — great to meet today, thanks for walking through Acme Health's streaming use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps below.

What I heard:
- Primary goal: reduce perceived latency for clinicians using patient summarization — target user-facing TTFT <= 250ms for short prompts (~64 tokens).
- Throughput: peak expected concurrency ~150 concurrent streaming sessions, with sustained average 60–80 qps during business hours.
- Streaming requirements: SSE preferred for browser clients; chunk cadence should be ~50–150ms between partial chunks to keep UI responsive.
- Fallback: degrade gracefully to non-streaming synchronous call when streaming unavailable.

Immediate asks from Acme:
1) Confirm whether Redwood can meet TTFT <= 250ms for the recommended model under 150 concurrent users (we'll provide perf numbers and suggested config).
2) Clarify chunk size/cadence constraints for SSE endpoints and recommended client-side buffering logic.
3) Share the SLO template and a quick test plan so you can validate in your staging environment.

Next steps (proposed):
- I'll loop in Dylan (SE) to run a short perf check against a representative prompt and confirm TTFT numbers and expected token cadence.
- We'll share the streaming SLO template (attached) and a suggested testing harness (simple k6 script + sample prompts).
- Schedule a technical ~30m follow-up this week to review results and finalize canary plan.

Proposed times: Wed 3/4 10:00–10:30am PT or Thu 3/5 11:00–11:30am PT. What works best?

Thanks — looking forward to lining this up.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>

Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Thanks Marissa — great summary. Wed 3/4 10am PT works for Priya and me. A couple clarifications before the call so we can prep: 

- The 250ms TTFT target is for the UI to render the first token to users after they hit submit (client-side measured). We care most about median but also want 95th percentile to be <500ms in peak.
- Concurrency: 150 is our upper bound during peak events; sustained is likely 60–80 as you noted.
- Chunk cadence: 50–150ms is ideal; however client-side we can handle bursts where cadence is slightly higher as long as first chunk is fast.

Please have Dylan include expected TTFT numbers for both:
A) hosted Redwood API (standard model + recommended batching settings)
B) dedicated/reserved capacity profile (if there’s a measurable improvement and what commit level that implies)

Also — can you confirm whether WebSocket socket-level keepalive/latency has different behavior compared to SSE in your runtime? We may prefer WS for mobile clients.

Looking forward to the perf numbers on Wed.

Best,
Alex
Senior Product Manager, Acme Health

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 11:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: TTFT & streaming SLOs — follow-up and next steps

Alex — looping in with preliminary numbers and an ask for representative prompts and token lengths. Outline below: 

Short summary of what I'll test (and why):
- Measure Time-to-first-token (TTFT) at client (browser) for a 64-token prompt using the hosted Redwood API with recommended batching disabled for low-latency paths, and with batching enabled to show tradeoffs.
- Test on a p99 network model (10ms median, 40ms p95 RTT) to approximate Acme office network.
- Measure chunk cadence delivered over SSE and WebSocket under varying concurrency (20, 60, 150 sessions).

Preliminary expectations (ballpark):
- Hosted (small-medium model, quantized): median TTFT ~120–220ms under low concurrency; at 150 concurrent sessions median may drift toward 200–350ms depending on batching/caching. p95 may approach 500–700ms unless we reserve capacity.
- Dedicated (reserved fleet, pinned model): median TTFT ~90–180ms at 150 concurrent, p95 <450ms with correct autoscaling and pre-warmed KV caches.
- Chunk cadence: runtime typically emits partial chunks as tokens are decoded; network jitter is main contributor. We can throttle chunk sizes to target ~50–150ms cadence by adjusting decoding buffer size and client-side aggregation.

Questions / asks for Acme before Wed: 
1) Can you share 3–5 representative prompts and expected token length distribution? (short, medium, long).
2) Are you able to run a simple client-side TTFT probe (we can provide a small script) in your staging to correlate with our server-side timings?

I'll bring concrete numbers from a short run against a representative prompt set in our Wed call.

—
Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
